lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: weekly routine and load balance

objective: Learners are modeled how to lay out a full week's real commitments across all five systems (planning, household, food, transportation, communication) in a day-by-day grid, then build their own real capstone-week grid and check it for overload, any day carrying three or more different-system demands, before the capstone week begins.
scenario: The task sheet walks through a sample week's grid showing where demands from different systems stack up on the same day, then the learner builds their own seven-day grid for the actual capstone week ahead, entering one real, specific commitment per system per day where it applies, and checks the result for overload.
safetyNotes: This weekly grid uses real upcoming commitments for planning purposes only; no commitment is confirmed, changed, or communicated to anyone outside the household as part of this lesson.
materials: paper or a document with a seven-day grid
the learner's real upcoming commitments for the capstone week

tasks.directions: Study the modeled sample week grid before building your own.

prompts.text: Which day in the modeled sample week has the most demands stacked on it, and what are they?

tasks.directions: Following the modeled example, fill in a seven-day grid with your own real, specific commitments for the capstone week ahead, including at least one entry per system where it applies.

prompts.text: I listed at least one planning-system commitment with a specific day and action (for example, a due date or a scheduled block of time).
I listed at least one household commitment with a specific day and action.
I listed at least one food commitment with a specific day and action.
I listed at least one transportation or appointment commitment with a specific day and action.
I listed at least one communication commitment with a specific day and action.

tasks.directions: Count the commitments on each day of your grid and check for overload, a single day carrying three or more demands from different systems.

prompts.text: Does any single day in your grid have three or more commitments from different systems stacked on it?
choices: Yes, at least one day is overloaded
No, my week is evenly spread

prompts.text: If a day was overloaded, name the specific item you moved and which day you moved it to. If not, explain how you counted to confirm your week is balanced.

tasks.directions: Think about what this load-balance check changed before the capstone week starts.

prompts.text: Explain one real conflict this load-balance check helped you catch before the capstone week begins, or, if you found none, explain what specifically you checked to be sure.

remediation: If a learner's grid entries are too vague to check for overload (for example, 'school stuff' with no day or action named), reteach by requiring every entry to name a specific action and a specific day before it can be counted in the overload check.
extension: Have the learner build a light backup version of one already-full day, cutting it down to the single most essential commitment and naming what would happen to the other commitments.
